text:
maria: Heads-up — I just saw a customer in Prod where their org dashboard showed embeddings usage from another tenant. This looks like a console scoping bug, not client-side.
kevin: oh no. repro steps?
maria: steps to repro I used:
```
1) login as user@org-A -> open /console/org-A/dashboards
2) switch to org-B quickly via org switcher
3) open same dashboard -> portions of the panel show org-A metrics (top-left card)
```
maria: observed twice in a row, different users.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: web-console v2.18.0 by ci/cd at 2026-03-18T10:12:03Z (commit e3f4c2b)
kevin: that deploy had the new cache refactor to improve panel load times, right?
samir: yeah I touched request-scoping/cache.js — I added a global LRU keyed on `cacheKey` computed in middleware. suspect key collision or stale tenant context during async work.
olivia: telemetry shows an increase in `dashboard.render.mismatched_tenant` traces since that deploy. sample trace: `{"trace_id":"t-9a7","org_id":"org-B","panel_id":"p-12","fetched_from_cache":true,"source_org":"org-A"}`
jun: can you paste the cacheKey computation?
samir: code snippet:```js
function makeCacheKey(req){
  return `${req.user.tenantId || req.headers['x-org-id']}:${req.path}:${hash(req.query)}`
}
```
samir: the root issue: `req.user` is populated async by token verification middleware that yields. changes in the refactor allowed handlers to read `makeCacheKey` after the async boundary while `req.user` could still be undefined and a fallback to header or previous value can leak across concurrent requests due to shared cache instance.
kevin: so multiple concurrent requests can compute identical keys when user not yet attached -> write to same cache entry -> bad.
olivia: impact estimate? how many orgs/users likely affected?
maria: customer reported 3 orgs, small % of panels. From telemetry we see ~0.03% of dashboard loads tagged mismatched over last 6 hours but customers affected are high-sensitivity.
jun: mitigation options: 1) disable sharing cache across requests (per-request cache) 2) make cacheKey only use a required header `x-org-id` and reject if missing 3) roll back v2.18.0
kevin: quick mitigation we can push: enforce that `makeCacheKey` throws if `req.user` is undefined and block cache reads until auth finishes. then flush global cache. Less risky than rollback.
samir: I can open the PR - add guard + instrument to log when cacheKey fallback occurs. Also namespace cache by `resolveTenantId(req)` which calls sync extraction from auth token (not req.user) or header.
trace-bot: trace created: trace-1776501248 for suspicious cache access pattern (linked to t-9a7)
jun: for immediate containment: flush cache on web-console instances, and add a temporary flag to disable cross-request LRU (feature flag: console.sharedCache=false).
maria: I've notified Support to check high-sensitivity customers and to surface any P1s.
olivia: preparing a quick dashboard that filters traces with `fetched_from_cache=true` and `source_org!=org_id`, will share link in 10m.
kevin: timeline pls: samir, can you get a PR up in 30m for guard + logging? jun, can you coordinate cache flush and flag in the infra? olivia, can you pin affected traces and notify customers?
samir: yes PR draft in 20m, tests included.
jun: infra runbook: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/web-console` after clearing redis namespace `console:shared:*`. I'll do a safe rolling restart to avoid blips.
kevin: if any sign of more widespread leakage, we rollback. but I prefer the guard + flush first.
maria: thanks. assign owners: samir (fix + tests), jun (cache flush + flag), olivia (telemetry + customer signals), kevin (incident lead).
samir: PR: https://git.example/r/redwood/web-console/pull/4872 (WIP)
olivia: pushed telemetry small dashboard: https://grafana.example/d/xyz/console-leak-hunt
kevin: good job catching this, team. keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
maria: will follow up once Support confirms customers notified.
trace-bot: alert resolved? no - elevated to P2 until guard is live.
kevin: closing loop: when guard is merged and rollout is finished, update thread with last_message_ts.
